request.neutral_instruction: Solve the supplied programming task. Return only the requested artifact. Do not call tools.
request.prompt:
Implement this complete Linux x86-64 command-line program.
Read a restricted ASCII CSV stream of at most 4096 bytes. The header must be exactly 'account,amount_cents
'. Then there are 0 through 128 records. Each record has one unsigned decimal account ID, one comma, and one decimal signed amount in cents. IDs are 0 through 63 inclusive. Amounts are [-1000000000,1000000000]. Amount syntax is optional '-' and one or more digits; '+' is forbidden. Leading zeroes and negative zero are allowed. No whitespace, CR, quotes, extra fields, blank records or other characters are allowed. Records are separated by LF; the last record's LF is optional. Header-only input is valid and produces empty output. Sum amounts per account using sufficient integer width. Output one line 'account,total
' for EVERY account that appeared, including total zero, in increasing numeric ID order; use canonical decimal. No output header. Valid input exits 0. Any malformed header, record, out-of-range field or excess record count must produce exactly 'ERR
' and exit 2 without partial totals. Example header plus '17,1250
42,-300
17,275
' produces '17,1525
42,-300
'.
The test uses a regular stdin file and EOF; each process handles one file. Stderr must always be empty. No files, network, external commands, testing, compiler, assembler or other tool use during generation. One final artifact only; no Markdown fences, explanations or placeholders.
Return complete C11 source with main, at most 32768 characters. Standard libc and POSIX read/write are available. No inline assembly, embedded executable bytes, external files or commands. The evaluator compiles with gcc -std=c11 -O2 -fno-pie -no-pie. Return source only.

cost_note: API equivalent at published standard rates, not measured subscription billing. CLI output usage is retained exactly; a separate reasoning breakdown may be unavailable.
